text:
tailwinds to its server CPU business we expect from agentic AI, as well as upside in
datacenter GPUs in 2027 and beyond.  First, we expect proliferation of agentic AI
in enterprise and consumer workloads to act as a medium-term tailwind to the
server CPU TAM, benefiting AMD.  We expect AMD to be an outsized beneficiary of
enterprise agentic AI adoption, where we see x86 having staying power as agents
interact with enterprises’ exiting x86 infrastructure.  Second, we see upside to
AMD’s datacenter GPU revenue in 2027 and beyond. We are most bullish on the 6
GW deployment opportunity at Meta, and we expect stable share at Microsoft -

text:
although we await more visibility into OpenAI’s deployments.  All in, our 2027/28 EPS
estimates are ~20% above the Street (VA), and we expect stock price
outperformance to be driven by positive estimate revisions. We continue to prefer
Buy-rated Broadcom and Nvidia on a relative basis, but we believe AMD presents a
compelling opportunity for exposure to agentic AI adoption via server CPUs. Our
view is summarized by the following key points:
 
 
 
 
n
Structural tailwinds from agentic AI. As framed in our report on agentic AI,
 
 
given the shift toward more inference workloads, we expect the server CPU TAM
to grow at an accelerated rate over the next five years, with the x86 architecture

server CPU market. Our 2027/28 server CPU revenue estimates of

n
We see upside to Datacenter GPU revenue estimates. We take a prudent
 
 
 
 
stance on AMD’s Datacenter GPU revenue opportunity, and we are bullish on the
6GW deployment opportunity at Meta. However, we take a measured approach
to modeling Microsoft (assuming stable share in accelerators) and OpenAI (we
model ~2GW deployment throughout 2030). Our 2027/28 Datacenter GPU

business

agenticAI workloads to represent 90% of overall tokens by 2030, with enterprise agentic
AI tokens representing ~50%%, and consumer agentic AI tokens representing 40%.
Between x86 and ARM based CPUs, we expect x86 based servers to retain a majority
share in enterprise agentic AI to drive better interoperability between AI agents and

We highlight five factors that summarize our bullish view on AMD’s server CPU
franchise:
 
 
n
Higher CPU attach rate in AI servers: As highlighted above, we have observed the
 
 
GPU:CPU attach rate move from 8:1 to 2:1 in the latest rack-level configurations, and
we expect this trend to continue in the same direction as industry transitions to
using CPU-only racks which complement GPU/ASIC racks.
 
 
n
Strong growth in AMD accelerators: We expect strong growth in AMD’s Datacenter
 
 
GPU shipments beginning in 2H26, and expect AMD’s AI racks to have a higher
source_file: data/inputs/reports/AMD/Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD)_ Upgrade to Buy as Agentic AI drives server CPU tailwinds; we see datacenter GPU upside in 2027 & beyond.pdf

text:
attach rate of AMD CPUs. We model AMD’s GPU units growing 66%/98% YoY in
2026/27.
 
n
Modernization of enteprise datacenters: As AI proliferates across the enterprise,
 
 
we have seen companies refresh their CPU fleets to optimize physical space and
power.  As agentic AI takes hold, we expect this trend of upgrading existing CPU
fleets to continue.
 
 
n
Higher core count driving higher ASPs: We expect agentic AI workloads to drive
 
 
 
 
 
higher core count utilization and performance requirements - driving upside to
server CPU units and ASPs as the industry transitions to new-generation offerings.
n
Continued share gains for AMD: We continue to expect AMD to gain incremental
source_file: data/inputs/reports/AMD/Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD)_ Upgrade to Buy as Agentic AI drives server CPU tailwinds; we see datacenter GPU upside in 2027 & beyond.pdf

text:
share in the server CPU market, especially in the enterprise where we see an outsized
benefit for x86-based CPUs relative to ARM - driven by better interoperability with
existing x86-based enterprise infrastructure
All in, we expect Server CPU TAM to grow at an accelerated pace over the next 3-5 years,
x86 as an architecture to be a key beneficiary especially for enterprise AI agents, and
AMD to continue to gain share in x86 and overall Server CPU market. Our 2027/28
server CPU revenue estimates of $21.1bn/$27.4bn are 24%/38% above Street (VA)
estimates.

GS Factor Profile
 
The Goldman Sachs Factor Profile provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our universe of rated stocks)

text:
and its sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth,
Financial Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for specific metrics for each stock. The
normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may
vary depending on the fiscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows:
source_file: data/inputs/reports/AMD/Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD)_ Upgrade to Buy as Agentic AI drives server CPU tailwinds; we see datacenter GPU upside in 2027 & beyond.pdf

text:
Growth is based on a stock’s forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for financial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a
higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock’s forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for financial
stocks, only ROE), with a higher percentile indicating a company with higher financial returns. Multiple is based on a stock’s forward-looking P/E, P/B,
price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for financial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile
source_file: data/inputs/reports/AMD/Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD)_ Upgrade to Buy as Agentic AI drives server CPU tailwinds; we see datacenter GPU upside in 2027 & beyond.pdf

text:
indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns
percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile).
Financial Returns and Multiple use the Goldman Sachs analyst forecasts at the fiscal year-end at least three quarters in the future. Growth uses inputs
for the fiscal year at least seven quarters in the future compared with the year at least three quarters in the future (on a per-share basis for all metrics).
